title: Compulsory third-party insurance opened to private insurers and price competition (South Australia)
summary: South Australia replaced its single public CTP insurer with four private insurers charging a common price from 1 July 2016, and let them compete on price from 1 July 2019.

instruments.title: Motor Vehicles Act 1959 (SA), Part 4 CTP insurance provisions as amended to open the market (amending Acts not checked)

commenced.what: Four approved private insurers began writing CTP at a common premium
Insurers could set their own premiums (price competition)

direction_rationale: Moving from a single public insurer to several private insurers, and then to price competition, should lower premiums and improve service through rivalry.
comparison: Victoria and Tasmania keep public monopoly insurers (TAC, MAIB); Queensland has private insurers with regulated premiums
confounders: premium bands set by the regulator

verified.notes: Dates from the SA CTP Regulator's notice.
